options.content:
## What this demo is
Four versions of the same system (Go, Python, Node.js and .NET), each with **worker → api → backend → PostgreSQL**, instrumented with the *otel-libs* libraries. The worker sends orders all the time, and some of them fail **on purpose** (duplicate order, rejected order, unhandled error, database key violation). These dashboards show **what is recorded when something fails**.

**The rule being proven:** the span keeps only the error **type** (`exception.type`); the **message** and the **stack** go to **one** correlated error log. Why: messages can hold sensitive data and are expensive to index in a trace; in the log they are searchable and under controlled retention.

| Item | What | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **A36** | **Database** errors: span with the type only, detail in one log | done (Go, Python, Node.js); .NET has the log, without `db.system.name` and SQLSTATE (parked) |
| **A37** | Same rule for **HTTP/gRPC/framework** spans | done (Go, Python, Node.js); .NET parked (C20/C21) |
| **A43** | In Go and .NET, the DB metric exemplar opens the **parent** span, not the database span | open gap |

## Quick glossary

| Term | In one sentence |
|---|---|
| **Trace** | The whole story of one request, from the worker to the database, with a unique `trace_id`. |
| **Span** | One step of that story (e.g. "POST /orders" in the api, "INSERT" in the database). It has a duration, a status (ok/error) and attributes. |
| **Span kind** | *server* = received the request; *client* = called another service or the database; *internal* = an internal step. |
| **Exception event** | An annotation inside the span saying an exception happened (`exception.type`, sometimes also the message and stack). |
| **Error log (record)** | A log line with severity ERROR sent to Loki. It can carry the same `trace_id`/`span_id` as the span. |
| **Correlated** | The log has `trace_id` and `span_id`: you can jump from the log to the trace and back. |
| **Exemplar** | A dot on a metric graph that keeps the `trace_id` of a real request in that bucket. Clicking it opens the trace. |
| **Sampling** | Not every trace is kept. Error logs are sent **even** when the trace is not, so their trace link can open an empty trace. |

panels.title: The four questions — answers for the selected range

options.content: **How to read the colors:** green = on target · orange = attention · red = off target. The numbers at the top use the range chosen in the time picker (default: last 1 hour).

panels.description:
**Question:** when a database operation fails, is there an error log with the message?

**Formula:** database error logs ÷ database spans with an error, over the range. **Target: 100%.**

The spans come from the Collector span metrics (exact counter difference over the range); the logs come from Loki. If a pod restarted inside the range, the counter resets and the number can exceed 100% — pick a range without restarts.

targets.expr: sum(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"demo-(${lang:pipe})-(api|backend|worker)", service_name=~"${service:pipe}", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_CLIENT", db_system_name="postgresql", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} - traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"demo-(${lang:pipe})-(api|backend|worker)", service_name=~"${service:pipe}", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_CLIENT", db_system_name="postgresql", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} offset $__range)

panels.title: A36 · database failures with a log

panels.description:
**Question:** does any server span still carry the error message (in the status description or the exception event) or the stack?

**Target: 0.** Go, Python and Node.js are done (A37); the remaining count is expected to come from .NET only (parked, C20/C21). Detail in dashboard 3.

targets.query: { resource.service.name =~ "demo-(${lang:pipe})-(api|backend|worker)" && resource.service.name =~ "${service:pipe}" && kind = server && (statusMessage != "" || event.exception.message != nil || event.exception.stacktrace != nil) } | count_over_time()

panels.title: A37 · server spans leaking error text

panels.description:
**Question:** is there an error log that cannot be linked to a trace?

**Target: 0.** Known source: Python's `uvicorn.error`, which writes the error after the span has ended. Detail in dashboard 2.
panels.title: Error logs without trace_id

panels.description:
**Question:** is the same error logged twice, once by the helper and once by the web server?

**Target: 0.** The A37 HOW-TO sections show how to turn these copies off in the application; a nonzero value means the demo app does not apply it. Detail in dashboard 2.
panels.title: Extra copies of the same error

panels.description: The four bars should be green and full (100%). A short bar = that language loses the detail of some database errors.

targets.expr: label_replace(sum by (service_name) (traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"demo-(${lang:pipe})-(api|backend|worker)", service_name=~"${service:pipe}", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_CLIENT", db_system_name="postgresql", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} - traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name=~"demo-(${lang:pipe})-(api|backend|worker)", service_name=~"${service:pipe}", span_kind="SPAN_KIND_CLIENT", db_system_name="postgresql", status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"} offset $__range), "lang", "$1", "service_name", "demo-([a-z]+)-.*")

sum by (lang, service_name) (count_over_time({service_name=~"demo-(${lang:pipe})-(api|backend|worker)", service_name=~"${service:pipe}"} | severity_number >= 17 | exception_type != "" | (db_system_name != "" or scope_name = "StaffOps.OtelHelper.Database") | label_format lang=`{{ regexReplaceAll "demo-([a-z]+)-.*" .service_name "$1" }}` [$__range]))

panels.title: A36 per language — database failures with a log

panels.description: Each bar is a service and span kind that still keeps a message or a stack. **Target: no bars.** Only `dotnet` bars are expected (.NET parked, C20/C21).

targets.query: { resource.service.name =~ "demo-(${lang:pipe})-(api|backend|worker)" && resource.service.name =~ "${service:pipe}" && (statusMessage != "" || event.exception.message != nil || event.exception.stacktrace != nil) } | count_over_time() by (resource.service.name, kind)

Tip: in any trace table, click the **Trace ID** to open the trace; inside the trace, the **Logs for this span** button shows the correlated error log. An error log from an **unsampled** span has a valid `trace_id` that Tempo does not have: its link opens an empty trace — filter those logs by `db_system_name` / `error_type` instead.
